claim: In [so great] a loss that we’re likely to go bankrupt the content clause is an indirect complement within the NP. It can be “further delayed so that it occurs later in the clause rather than within the NP”.
evidence_summary: Ch. 11, p. 967: the content clause is delayed to the end of the matrix clause, and “This position is obligatory”. It stars So many people that we had to move to a larger room enrolled for the course and analyses the clause as a complement in clause structure.
finding: The two chapters place the so clause in different constituents. The Ch. 5 generalization holds for comparatives and for too (Ch. 14, pp. 1262–1263). Which analysis is correct is a separate question.
proposed_wording: Reconcile with Ch. 11, §4.6, where a content clause licensed by so occurs at the end of the matrix clause.
inference: Can a so-licensed content clause occur inside the NP?

evidence.establishes: An internal conflict, with the Ch. 11 star as the deciding case.
evidence.note: Local source (working note, unpublished draft or local copy); not online.
